_comment: Machine-readable half of the fork merge inventory. Paths, verdicts, tripwires
and convergence rules live HERE and nowhere else; upstream-merge-inventory.md
carries the narrative that cannot be checked (the re-application Deltas, the
Every path in this file is checked against upstream/main and HEAD by
catches an entry going stale: an `ours` path upstream has started shipping, or
a `decide`/`converged` path upstream renamed out from under a fork delta.
Run it before every merge; it is step 0 of the skill.

verdicts.ours: Take the fork side wholesale. Legitimate ONLY when the path does not exist in upstream/main.
verdicts.theirs-verbatim: Take upstream exactly, and investigate why a fork delta reappeared.
verdicts.converged: Take upstream wholesale, then re-apply only the listed fork delta.
verdicts.decide: No cached verdict. Read upstream's side every merge and decide it there.

concerns.name: Authentication and session
concerns.forkPosition: Moatless cookie session and /login; no T3 backend session.
concerns.upstreamAddition: Do not adopt upstream auth work.

concerns.name: Client / device identity
concerns.upstreamAddition: Do not adopt; check deleted surfaces.

concerns.name: Dev-server origin and proxy
concerns.forkPosition: Upstream single-origin dev plus fork proxy-target override.
concerns.upstreamAddition: Adopt upstream, then re-apply the fork delta.

concerns.name: Backend contract
concerns.forkPosition: The client may assume only what Moatless implements; see docs/internals/client-server-contract.md.
concerns.upstreamAddition: Adopt only if Moatless implements it.

concerns.name: Electron / desktop
concerns.forkPosition: Kept in tree; not a compliance target.
concerns.upstreamAddition: Take upstream; do not spend merge effort making desktop work.

sweep.note: Widen the pattern when a concern grows vocabulary it does not cover. Keyword hits are a starting list, not a verdict — most are false positives and are recorded as such in the tracker.

offRepo.note: Every other workflow inherited from upstream is disabled in GitHub, not in the tree. A workflow upstream adds later arrives active, so this check fails AFTER a merge rather than before one. Disable a new one with: gh workflow disable <name> --repo soaplabs/t3code

deletedUpstreamPaths.note: Upstream owns these and the fork's side is deletion. An upstream edit raises a delete/modify conflict, and taking upstream silently restores the file. The tripwire script asserts this list is exactly what `git diff --diff-filter=D --name-only upstream/main HEAD` reports.

unsupportedMethodExceptions.reason: It is upstream's own server that refuses this method, not Moatless, so the derivation reads backwards: it sees the backend serving `scripts.run` and calls the union entry unreachable, when that entry is what keeps `apps/server` compiling and behaving as upstream does.
unsupportedMethodExceptions.retiredWhen: `apps/server` stops answering `scripts.run` with `UnsupportedMethodError` — at which point delete this entry and let the DROP stand.
unsupportedMethodExceptions.see: inventory `host-run-scripts`, and 'A script runs on the backend' in gaps.md

unsupportedMethodExceptions.reason: A subtask is a Moatless concept and upstream has no task tree, so `apps/server` answers the method with `UnsupportedMethodError` unconditionally while Moatless dispatches it. The derivation reads backwards for the same reason `scripts.run` does.
unsupportedMethodExceptions.retiredWhen: Upstream grows a thread tree, or the method leaves the contract — at which point delete this entry and let the DROP stand.
unsupportedMethodExceptions.see: inventory `hosted-env-contract`, and 'A subtask is a Moatless concept' in gaps.md

unsupportedMethodExceptions.reason: Upstream's client learns which threads exist from `orchestration.subscribeShell` and nowhere else, which is exact for `apps/server`, so it refuses a thread fetched by id while Moatless dispatches it. Same backwards derivation as `subtasks.list`.
unsupportedMethodExceptions.retiredWhen: `apps/server` stops answering `threads.getShell` with `UnsupportedMethodError` — at which point delete this entry and let the DROP stand.
unsupportedMethodExceptions.see: inventory `unlisted-thread-adoption`, and 'A thread outside the listing is a Moatless idea' in gaps.md

unsupportedMethodExceptions.reason: Moatless dispatches `pullRequests.summary` and nothing else in the family, but the method shares `PullRequestRpcError` with `pullRequests.list`, `pullRequests.detail` and `pullRequests.activity`, which it does not dispatch. Splitting a private union off for one method costs more fork delta than an entry the client never receives.
unsupportedMethodExceptions.retiredWhen: Moatless dispatches the rest of the family, or `pullRequests.summary` takes an error union of its own — at which point delete this entry and let the DROP stand.

pathPolicy.note: Keep the Moatless cookie session. Upstream owns this file and changes the environment layer around it; take those changes and re-state the fork's session behavior on top.
Keep cookie session behavior, the x-csrf-token echo Moatless requires on unsafe requests, and the absent same-origin gate. Take upstream's transport changes.
Fork-only /login.
Keep fork auth coverage. Upstream owns this file; take its harness and assertion changes and keep the fork's cases beside them.
Take upstream, then apply Web Vite Delta.

CLAUDE.md is a symlink to it. Keep the fork's slimmed shape and its This fork section. Upstream owns and edits this file: read its version for new facts — surfaces, commands, paths, sharp edges — and re-state those in the fork's voice rather than taking upstream's prose.
Fork docs, this inventory, the tracker and the gaps register.
The fork's two skills: merging upstream, and testing the web client against a Moatless backend. Upstream owns the other skills in .agents/skills/ and adds more.

Take theirs, then re-apply the scope note at the top of each. Both describe the bundled T3 server, which the fork's web client does not use; the note is a few lines routing readers to test-moatless-web and is deliberately the whole delta, so upstream's edits to these docs land unopposed.
Fork-authored user and internals docs.

Upstream deleted .plans/** entirely on 2026-08-20 (PR #7665, "move implementation plans out of repository"), so nothing upstream owns lives under this path anymore. The 2026-08-20 merge took upstream's deletion cleanly (the fork had not touched those files, so it was a non-conflicting delete) and left only the four fork-authored plans: moatless-adapter.md, moatless-convergence.md, preview-servers-in-t3-web.md, completed/moatless-admin-in-t3.md. Was two entries (fork-authored-plans: ours, upstream-plans: theirs) until upstream's deletion made the split moot.

Fork's Moatless connections/apps/GitHub admin page. Upstream independently added an unrelated embedded-surface settings page at this same path on 2026-08-26 (add/add conflict, no common ancestor) — that content now lives at apps/web/src/routes/settings.browser.tsx instead of here. Keep ours at this path every merge; diff upstream's file and port anything substantive into settings.browser.tsx. See settings-browser-relocation.
Take upstream exactly; investigate any re-grown fork delta.

Conflicts on every merge, and is never resolved by hand: `git checkout --theirs pnpm-lock.yaml` then `vp i`, which re-derives the fork's own edges (today, the `@t3tools/moatless-api` workspace dependency in apps/web/package.json). Hand-merging it produces a lockfile that matches neither side's resolution and installs something no one chose. The install is also what the merge needs before `regen-route-tree.mjs` or `merge-stats.mjs` can run.

Thread-server and sandbox lifecycle surfaces. None of these exist upstream. The thread-server UI components listed here until 2026-08-08 (apps/web/src/components/servers/**, added in #13) are gone; what renders a ThreadServer now lives under components/preview/ and is covered by fork-preview-files.
The last two are the host half of the preview annotation protocol for a framed page — upstream annotates over ipcRenderer into a <webview> preload and has no postMessage equivalent to converge on.
Everything under browser/ except the fork-only files above. Take upstream and re-state the hosted-preview behavior from the Hosted web preview inventory entry on top.

Each renders or reasons about ThreadServer, a Moatless concept upstream does not have. PreviewFrameMoreMenu.tsx is a deliberate sibling of upstream's PreviewMoreMenu.tsx, not a fork of it — keep upstream's file at zero delta.

Everything under components/preview/ except the fork-only files above. Take upstream and re-state the hosted-preview behavior on top. PreviewEmptyState.tsx and PreviewView.tsx are upstream's files carrying fork deltas. (PreviewChromeRow.test.tsx carried a fork delta until upstream removed it as a static-markup-only test in #9364, taken on the 2026-09-03 merge.)

Fork-only: the sandbox right-panel surface, the status control's hosts, surfaceNeedsSandbox, and sandboxControl.placement.test.tsx. None of it exists upstream. The test is fork-only but renders upstream's RightPanelTabs, so upstream restructuring that component breaks it with no conflict — it is the intended failure, not a stale test.

Take upstream, then re-apply the fork's right-panel deltas: the 'sandbox' RightPanelKind and its store action, the Sandbox entry in the surface launcher and the tab-bar '+' menu, the sandboxControl indicator riding that entry, and the per-surface gating described in the Sandbox lifecycle controls and Sandbox right-panel surface inventory entries. Upstream restructures the launcher — it went from cards to compact rows in #11111 — so the delta is what must survive, not a hunk to replay: put the indicator back on whatever element opens the Sandbox surface, additively, without threading a prop or re-indenting upstream's JSX.

Upstream's file. Re-add the four fork subscription tags to EnvironmentSubscriptionRpcTag: subscribeServerStatus, serversSubscribeLogs, sandboxSubscribeStatus and sandboxSubscribeDetail. The conflict here is additive on both sides every time upstream adds a stream of its own, so keep both blocks — this merge collided with upstream's subscribeDeviceState.

Upstream's component, carrying the fork's useSupportsMultiplePullRequests gate and the popover that lists a Task's several links (inventory entry task-bound-pull-request). Upstream keeps changing what the badge means without changing its types — #11104 and #11180 made the count the total linked rather than the extras beside a named primary, and hoisted `state` onto both badge shapes — so the fork test is the only thing that catches it. A changed expectation here is upstream's semantics, not a fork regression; re-read the badge before editing the assertion.
Take upstream, then re-apply UnsupportedMethodError, its unsupported-method error unions, and servers.* wiring. Recompute the unions — never hand-edit.
Take upstream, then re-add the hosted-environment method entries: servers.*, sandbox.status, sandbox.start, and sandbox.stop.

The surface-gating registry, the mobile touch modules, and the mermaid diagram renderer. (The generic file-attachment presentation, fileAttachments.tsx, converged into upstream's own image/file/video attachment support and was deleted.)

Take upstream, then apply Mermaid Diagram Delta. Upstream owns this file and works in it steadily; the delta is two imports and one early return above upstream's own return in the `pre` renderer, and must not re-indent upstream's block. If upstream has started rendering mermaid itself, drop the delta rather than porting it.
Fork-only mapping from a message origin to its chip. Written for a concept upstream does not have.
Take upstream, then apply Message Origin Delta. MessagesTimeline.tsx is a file upstream works in steadily; the delta is additive and must not re-indent upstream blocks.

Take upstream, then apply Thread Fork Delta. MessagesTimeline.tsx and orchestration.ts also carry the Message Origin Delta; both must survive. decider.ts's hunk is a deliberate refusal — the bundled server has no fork session to resume.

Fork-only test for the bundled server's thread.fork refusal, and the dialog the hover icon opens (same-sandbox toggle, initial message). apps/web/src/fork/threadFork.ts and its test are already covered by the fork-registry entry's apps/web/src/fork/** glob.

Take upstream, then apply Thread Visibility Delta. orchestration.ts, commands.ts, threadCommands.ts and decider.ts also carry the Thread Fork Delta; both must survive. The menu item goes directly above archive, which puts it inside upstream's tail: its "groups project settings with utility actions before archive" test asserts archive is two items after copy, and "keeps archive last" asserts archive carries the group separator. Both need the fork's one-item shift re-applied. decider.ts's hunk is a deliberate refusal: the bundled server has no per-thread read grant to move.

Take upstream, then apply Thread Follow Delta. Every path here also carries the Thread Visibility Delta and most carry the Thread Fork Delta; all must survive. The menu item goes directly below the visibility item and above archive, so upstream's archive-tail tests need the fork's two-item shift re-applied. decider.ts's hunk is a deliberate refusal: the bundled server lists every thread it stores and has no per-viewer listing to move one into.

Take upstream, then apply Thread Owner Name Delta. Both paths carry the Thread Visibility and Thread Follow Deltas as well; all must survive. The field is on OrchestrationThreadShell only, beside `visibility`, and the row hunk is two elements inside `SidebarThreadRow`'s card meta line and its tooltip — additive, and outside upstream's aria-hidden icon cluster.

Take upstream, then apply Mobile Touch Delta. Sidebar.tsx (upstream's default sidebar since 2026-08-08, formerly SidebarV2.tsx) also carries the Navigation gates delta and the pinned-before-settled ordering (a pinned thread never classifies as settled — pin is a sort order, not a settlement input; see 'Settlement rules Moatless owns' in gaps.md); all must survive.

Upstream owns this file and works in it steadily. Two fork deltas to re-state on top: the browser frame keyed on the page's own bytes (frameRevision, from browserPreviewFrameRevision) instead of on the workspace mutation id, and following the path the read resolved to (onRetargetFile) so a mention into a subdirectory repository lands on the file actually shown.
Fork-only workflows.
Moatless loop and workspace definitions. Upstream has no .moatless/ and runs its automation as GitHub workflows.
The one exception to the entry below. Take upstream, then re-apply the single `Check the Moatless API description is current` step in the check job. Nothing else in this file is fork-owned.

Everything else under .github/workflows/. Upstream's files byte for byte, including workflows upstream adds later. They are switched off in GitHub, not in the tree, so there is no delta to preserve. Any fork delta here means someone edited a workflow — investigate before taking it.

inventory.name: Moatless cookie session
inventory.mustSurvive: The browser authenticates by Moatless cookie session, there is no T3 backend session exchange, /login is the entry point, and an unsafe request echoes the moatless_csrf cookie in x-csrf-token or Moatless 403s it. Only login.tsx is fork-only; the rest are decide — upstream owns them and keeps changing the environment layer they sit in.

inventory.name: Proxy target, allowed hosts, dev pins
inventory.mustSurvive: Converged; apply only Web Vite Delta.

inventory.name: Upstream workflows switched off
inventory.mustSurvive: No workflow inherited from upstream runs in this fork. Enforced in GitHub as state: disabled_manually, not in the tree — see offRepo.

inventory.name: Agent instructions
inventory.mustSurvive: The file says this is a fork of pingdotgg/t3code, what the fork changes, and that fork-upstream-merge governs ownership questions; and it stays short enough to be read in full. It also carries the fork's surgical-change rules: fork code says so in a comment, and reaches upstream files through an additive hook. Resolve conflicts by fact, not by hunk.

inventory.name: Fork documentation and plans
inventory.mustSurvive: Keep ours. Only those four plans are ours; upstream owns the rest of .plans/**, and only fork-upstream-merge and test-moatless-web are ours under .agents/skills/.

inventory.name: Moatless loops
inventory.mustSurvive: Fork-only. .moatless/loops/upstream-merge/LOOP.md is what schedules this merge, and `moat repos sync-config` reconciles both files from the default branch. Moatless keys a synced loop on the directory name, so renaming the directory creates a second loop and orphans the one an administrator activated. The loop's `workspace:` names the `T3 Code Fork` entry in .moatless/workspaces.json by its display name, so renaming that entry skips the loop on the next sync.

inventory.name: Hosted-environment contract group
inventory.mustSurvive: Keep fork methods: server list, server status subscription, server log subscription, sandbox status, sandbox status subscription, sandbox start, sandbox stop, and subtasks.list. Keep sandbox lifecycle schemas separate from server list schemas. sandbox.subscribeStatus is gated on the sandboxStatusPush capability: absent, the client polls sandbox.status instead, so both paths have to keep working. subtasks.ts and threadShellLookup.ts are fork-only, and subtasks.list and threads.getShell each keep their UnsupportedMethodError union entry for as long as apps/server refuses the method, whatever unsupported-methods.mjs reports. threads.getShell returns the listing's own OrchestrationThreadShell and must keep doing so: a thread fetched by id has to be indistinguishable from the same thread delivered by the listing.

inventory.name: Server state in client runtime
inventory.mustSurvive: Keep fork server, sandbox lifecycle and subtask state surfaces separate. sandbox exposes both status (polled query, the fallback) and statusStream (the pushed subscription); dropping either leaves one class of server without a live indicator. The subscription tag is also listed in EnvironmentSubscriptionRpcTag in rpc/client.ts, an upstream file. subtasks is a query on a refresh interval, not a subscription: a child task settles at the pace of a task, not of a container probe. threadShellLookup is a query with no refresh at all: it is how the client learns a row the listing never sent, and once it has one nothing is pushing changes to re-read.

inventory.name: Subtasks section in the agents panel
inventory.mustSurvive: The agents panel has two sections against Moatless: the child threads this thread spawned, and upstream's subagent fleet. Only AgentsPanel.tsx is upstream's, and the whole fork delta there is one import, one useThreadSubtasks call above the empty-state return, the empty-state copy, and two elements in the scroll area. Everything else lives in fork/SubtasksSection.tsx, which mirrors AgentsPanel's STATUS_VISUALS classes on purpose rather than importing them.

inventory.name: Threads the shell listing does not carry
inventory.mustSurvive: A Moatless shell listing is the open work a viewer follows, not every thread there is, so closed threads, threads followed by someone else, and subtasks all open by URL while absent from it. Three deltas hold that together and each is small in an upstream file. threadRoutes.ts takes an optional serverThreadAwaitingFirstAnswer that defaults to upstream's rule, so 'no shell row' stops meaning 'gone' before the environment has answered — without it the route redirects to / on the first frame of every unlisted thread. state/threads.ts passes adoptedEnvironmentSnapshotAtom where upstream passes environmentSnapshotAtom, which is the whole graft hook. SettingsPanels.tsx makes an archived row's title a link, because unarchiving was the only way back into a thread you may already read. The store in fork/adoptedThreadShells.ts must keep deciding what is missing against the listing's snapshot rather than the grafted one.

inventory.name: Servers view in right panel
inventory.mustSurvive: Keep fork UI unless upstream ships an equivalent. The dedicated components/servers/ directory is gone — server rendering folded into components/preview/.

inventory.name: Hosted web preview
inventory.mustSurvive: Preview renders in a hosted iframe rather than a native browser surface, and a frame that loaded before its server was serving is replaced when the server reaches started (useFramedServerReload in PreviewView.tsx — a webview reloads itself, a frame does not). Upstream owns most files and works in them; take upstream and re-state the iframe behavior on top. Also surviving (2026-08-07): a framed page can be annotated — four gates on the existing framed flag in PreviewView.tsx, each // Fork: marked and additive. Drop the whole delta once upstream ships a web preview.

inventory.name: Upstream-server hosted-env stubs
inventory.mustSurvive: Converged; re-add servers.*, sandbox.status, sandbox.start, and sandbox.stop entries. Drop these first if upstream ships server-shaped support.

inventory.name: Sandbox lifecycle controls
inventory.mustSurvive: Keep the start/status control and per-surface sandbox gating until upstream has an environment lifecycle capability the web client can use. A stopped sandbox closes only the surfaces that live inside the workspace (browser, terminal, files, diff); Agents is served by the environment and stays open, and Sandbox stays open because it is where a stopped one is started, so the launcher is never curtained wholesale and the disabled state stands only in front of an active surface that needs the workspace. surfaceNeedsSandbox in sandbox/sandboxSurfaces.ts is the single split, read by both the launcher cards and the tab-bar '+' menu so they cannot disagree. A browser tab is gated on the page it holds and not on its kind alone: openFileInPreview opens an HTML or PDF file at the environment's own /api/assets route, which reads the workspace snapshot, so that tab stays open with the sandbox stopped while a tab on a server inside the sandbox and the empty tab are gated. resolveActiveSurfaceNeedsSandbox holds that rule and RightPanelTabs reads the origin to compare against from the environmentHttpBaseUrl prop SandboxedRightPanelTabs supplies; without it a file someone can read in the file surface is curtained in the browser beside it. The status indicator renders inside the panel body, on the launcher card and the '+' menu row that open the Sandbox surface, not in the tab bar, whose right end belongs to upstream's layout toggles; it holds no button of its own, because both hosts are themselves buttons. sandboxControl.placement.test.tsx pins that placement, which nothing type-checks. useSandboxAvailability picks the pushed subscription over the polled read on the sandboxStatusPush capability; without one of the two the indicator goes stale the moment a sandbox moves while the panel is open. The `moat cmd` commands the sandbox status carries are surfaced twice, gated on the sandboxCommands capability: SandboxCommandsBadge beside the status pill, and useSandboxCommandsBanner as a composer banner in ChatView so a command running behind an ended turn is visible when the right panel is collapsed. The agent reports idle while such a command runs, so without these a mid-build thread reads as finished. Both compute elapsed on the client from startedAtUnixMs — the server never sends a duration, which would make the status change on every poll.

inventory.name: Sandbox right-panel surface
inventory.mustSurvive: Keep the 'sandbox' RightPanelKind and everything behind it until upstream has a machine to describe. sandbox.detail is deliberately a second projection beside sandbox.status rather than more keys on it: every client holds the status subscription open for its indicator, and only the one client with the panel open should pay for the wider read. Every runtime-sourced key is absent rather than empty, and the panel drops the section instead of rendering a blank one; a docker-compose deployment publishes no containers and no events, so it shows Status, Image, Idle stop, Commands and Servers alone. The whole surface is gated on the sandboxDetail capability, and the contract file is fork-only so the schema stays out of a file every upstream merge touches. The Servers section carries no per-server restart because the backend serves none; pod-granularity restart is the Status section's Restart button.

inventory.name: UnsupportedMethodError
inventory.mustSurvive: Keep error class until upstream has optional/unsupported method semantics.

inventory.name: Unsupported-method error unions
inventory.mustSurvive: Keep one entry per Moatless-unserved method. Recompute with scripts/unsupported-methods.mjs; never hand-edit.

inventory.name: Surface-gating registry
inventory.mustSurvive: Keep as the only source of fork surface flags. Unknown route/action keys default enabled; tests must read upstream keys rather than restating them.

inventory.name: Chat surface gates
inventory.mustSurvive: Re-apply additive gates only. PanelLayoutControls.tsx left this entry when the fork took the terminal-drawer button back: the file is upstream's byte for byte again, so a merge has nothing to re-apply there.

inventory.name: Persisted panel gating
inventory.mustSurvive: Keep migrate disposal for hidden/unknown surfaces. The fork's generic unknown-kind drop subsumes upstream's per-kind removals.

inventory.name: Mobile touch affordances
inventory.mustSurvive: The left sidebar is a drawer the finger drags in from the screen edge, and a long press on a thread row reaches Settle, Snooze, rename and archive. The three fork/ modules are ours; the four upstream files are converged — see Mobile Touch Delta. The drawer must not become a modal <dialog>: that makes document.body inert, and the menus it exists to open portal there.

inventory.name: Message origin
inventory.mustSurvive: A message that reached the thread through an adapter or from another Task says so, and a message typed into the composer renders exactly as upstream renders it. The contract field is optional rather than nullable so the absent case stays byte-identical to upstream's payload.

inventory.name: Fork a thread from the chat
inventory.mustSurvive: Hovering an assistant message with a completed or interrupted turn shows a fork icon beside the copy button. While the thread's newest turn is still running, the icon stays visible on messages from an earlier, already-ended turn and hides only on messages from that running turn itself — cutting below the open turn is allowed, cutting at or into it is not, matching the backend's own gate. `parseMoatlessTurnNumber` (`apps/web/src/fork/threadFork.ts`) reads the turn number off the wire `TurnId` to compare; either turn number failing to parse hides the icon. Clicking it opens a dialog rather than forking immediately: a same-sandbox toggle (on by default — it is the only checkout that resumes this conversation, and the dialog says so when switched off) and an optional first message. There is no branch control — a fork always runs on its source's branch. Confirming mints a thread id client-side, dispatches `thread.fork` with that id, the source thread's id, the hovered message's turn number, and the dialog's fields, then navigates to the new thread the same way starting a thread from a proposed plan does — same wait-for-started-thread and cleanup-on-failure path. Moatless is the only backend that runs `thread.fork`; the bundled server refuses it rather than fabricate a session-less copy.

inventory.name: Toggle a thread's visibility from its row menu
inventory.mustSurvive: Right-clicking a thread in the sidebar, or opening the chat header's menu, offers one visibility item: "Make public" on a private thread and "Make private" on a public one. The label is the only indicator — a sidebar row shows no badge — so it names the level the click moves to, not the one the thread is on. It sits directly above "Archive thread" and opens that group, so it carries the group's separator and `archive` gives it up while the item is present. Going public confirms first (`confirmAndSetThreadVisibility` in useThreadActions.ts, shared by both surfaces); going private dispatches straight away. Only that direction confirms because public is not read-only on Moatless: `ScopeContext::can_control` treats it as the whole of the control grant, so a public thread hands every signed-in viewer its turns, terminal, scripts and sandbox. The confirmation copy says so, and must keep saying so. The item is gated on the `threadVisibility` capability, which covers both halves: the `thread.visibility.set` command and the `visibility` field on a thread row that the label reads. A server sending neither leaves the item out rather than showing a control it cannot label. The level is sent whole rather than toggled, so two clients that disagree about the current value cannot flip each other's write. Moatless carries visibility on the Task itself and keeps writes with the owner, so a public reader's toggle is refused; the bundled server refuses the command outright. LegacySidebar.tsx builds its own menu array and is deliberately left without the item.

inventory.name: Opening a thread by link follows it; the row menu unfollows it
inventory.mustSurvive: A Moatless listing is the open work a viewer follows, so a thread reached by link is readable and absent from the sidebar at the same time. Opening one follows it: `useAutoFollowThread` in fork/unlistedThread.ts dispatches `thread.follow` once per thread from the thread route, and the row stays in the sidebar after the route closes. Four conditions bound it, and each one is a bug that does not happen. It fires once per ref and never again after an unfollow, because the row menu's Unfollow acts on the thread the viewer is looking at and a re-follow on the next render would make that item do nothing. It decides against the listing's own snapshot rather than the grafted one, for the reason `missingThreadIds` gives — the graft is what put the thread on screen. It waits for a non-null snapshot, because a listing that has not answered yet was about to carry the thread. It skips a thread with an `archivedAt`, because the sidebar filters on `archivedAt === null` and a followed closed thread would be a follow with no row to unfollow it from. The way out is "Unfollow thread" in the per-thread menu, directly below the visibility item and above "Archive thread", on both surfaces `buildThreadActionMenuItems` serves; it opens the archive group when the visibility item is absent. It dispatches `thread.unfollow` with no confirmation, because the thread keeps running and only this viewer's listing changes. Both halves are gated on the `threadFollow` capability, so a server without it follows nothing and offers no item. Moatless makes the follow row the listing's membership (`Reach::Followed` over `task_follows`) and records a listing change on each write, so the sidebar updates live for that viewer alone; the bundled server refuses both commands.

inventory.name: A sidebar row names its owner when that is somebody else
inventory.mustSurvive: A Moatless sidebar lists work other people started — a public Task, a Task an admin can read, a Task followed by opening its link — so a row that is not yours says whose it is. `ownerName` on `OrchestrationThreadShell` carries the display name, and the card row shows it on the meta line directly left of the environment and provider glyphs, truncated, with the whole name on the owner line of the row tooltip. The server decides when to send it: the client is never told which user it is signed in as, so Moatless emits the name only when the Task's owner — the access rule's own `COALESCE(owner_user_id, created_by)` — is not the viewer, and null otherwise. Absence and null both mean "yours, or a server that does not send it", so no capability gates this: a row with no name renders exactly as it did before. The slim settled and snoozed rows are deliberately left without it; they carry no provider glyph either, and their point is a quiet tail.

inventory.name: A thread's pull requests are the Task's bindings
inventory.mustSurvive: Every pull-request surface is upstream's. Moatless fills `thread.pullRequests` from the Task's GitHub bindings, reports the `threadPullRequests` capability and dispatches `thread.pull-request.link` and `.unlink`, so `ThreadPullRequestBadgeControl`, the `pull-requests` stack tab and `useSupportsMultiplePullRequests` answer with no fork delta behind them. It orders the array, and its first element is the primary that `linkedPullRequest` also carries for a client from before the capability. Do not re-derive a thread's pull request from the checked-out branch: `tasks.branch` holds the base picked at creation while the agent commits on whatever branch it cut, so a `refName` match reports nothing for most threads that have one. Do not re-decide the primary on the client either; the server settles it from the bindings. One line of `mergeEnvironmentThread` is the whole delta on the data path: the shell speaks for `pullRequests`, where upstream keeps the detail's. A Task's bindings change while its thread is open and Moatless emits no `thread.pull-request-linked` — a binding write records a listing change and the shell row is re-sent — so nothing folds a change into the detail and a detail loaded before a binding changed keeps the old set for as long as the tab lives. Take the shell's array whole, including an empty one: an unlink leaves the shell reporting none, and a detail that kept its stale set would outlive the unlink. See `docs/fork/gaps.md`, _A pull request link is a listing change, not an event_. The composer footer's badge is the second delta: with more than one link and no stack, `ThreadPullRequestBadgeControl` opens a popover holding `ThreadPullRequestsMiniList` — the list the sidebar already shows on hover — with each row a link to its own pull request. Upstream's badge is an anchor to the primary there, and the `+N` beside it names the rest with nothing behind it. A Task binds every pull request its agent opened and they rarely share a base, so `resolveThreadPullRequestChains` reports one chain each and the stack badge, which does open a surface, is the case Moatless almost never has. The sidebar badge is untouched: its row already hovers the same list, and a stack still opens the `pull-requests` panel from both surfaces.

inventory.name: Host-run project scripts
inventory.mustSurvive: scripts.run asks the environment to run a project's script in its own sandbox, hosted in a named terminal, returning that terminal and the URL of any port it publishes. Gated on the workspaceScripts capability: absent, runProjectScript keeps upstream's client-driven terminal.open + terminal.write path byte-for-byte, so a T3 server behaves exactly as upstream. The rpc.ts union entry is the one documented exception to unsupported-methods.mjs's DROP advice — it is upstream's OWN server that refuses this method, not Moatless, so the derivation reports it backwards once the backend half publishes. Keep it while apps/server answers with UnsupportedMethodError; see 'A script runs on the backend' in gaps.md. A SandboxNotRunningError from scripts.run is answered rather than reported: startSandboxForScript starts the thread's sandbox, polls sandbox.status until ready, and re-runs once. Upstream has nothing to start, so a merge that loses this turns an idle-reaped sandbox back into a dead end. A script run from a draft has no thread to run in, so runProjectScript sends thread.create under the id the draft already holds before anything else, carrying the fork-only provision: true on ThreadCreateCommand in orchestration.ts. Moatless gives a thread created with no first message no sandbox until a turn is sent, and a script run is not a turn; without the flag the run reaches a thread that has nowhere to run, and every script pays startSandboxForScript's start-and-poll before it does anything. The draft route navigates to the created thread on its own, so the create is the whole delta. That create takes its modelSelection from the composer's send context, not from the draft thread, which carries the project default or the empty-model NO_PROVIDER_MODEL_SELECTION placeholder: the placeholder fails the contract's own TrimmedNonEmptyString before dispatch, and Moatless fixes a thread's agent at creation and refuses any later switch, so the create has to pin the agent the person's first message will ask for.

inventory.name: Project-script editing capability
inventory.mustSurvive: A project's scripts can be edited only when the backend says so per workspace: a git-synced workspace owns its scripts in .moatless/workspaces.json and is projected read-only, a manual one is writable. That answer rides the wire as scriptsEditable on OrchestrationProject / OrchestrationProjectShell, threaded to ProjectScriptsControl and the settings Actions section as an `editable` prop that gates the per-script Edit button, the t3.json import items and the Add action. Upstream extracted the row list into ProjectActionsList.tsx on 2026-09-07, so the Edit gate now lives there behind an `editable` prop that defaults to upstream's always-editable behavior; upstream then moved the Actions section itself out of ProjectSettingsPanel.tsx into ProjectActionsSettings.tsx on 2026-09-10, which is where scriptsEditable is now derived and where upstream's Reset button, which writes, is gated. It is NOT a FEATURES flag — projectScriptEditing was deleted when the capability arrived, because the answer varies per deployment and per workspace. Running a script stays ungated: a read-only workspace still runs what it declares, and ProjectScriptsControl's no-primary-script branch returns null only when editing is also off. A merge that reintroduces FEATURES.projectScriptEditing or an always-on Add action has taken upstream's side back.

inventory.name: Project-script port field
inventory.mustSurvive: The script editor sets a numeric Port, not upstream's free-text Preview URL: a script in a remote sandbox has no localhost to point at, so the host publishes the port and returns the real external URL when the script runs (scripts.run). ProjectScript carries port (1..65535); the editor's Port input replaces the Preview URL input and auto-open toggle, and buildProjectScript derives autoOpenPreview from the port's presence. previewUrl / autoOpenPreview stay on the contract for wire-compatibility but the fork's UI never writes a URL. The row badge in ProjectActionsList.tsx reads `preview · :<port>` where upstream reads `preview · desktop only` off previewUrl. Importing a t3.json script in ProjectActionsSettings.tsx runs the free-text previewUrl through portFromPreviewUrl so the import keeps a port rather than a URL. A merge that restores the Preview URL input has dropped the port.

inventory.name: Moatless branding
inventory.mustSurvive: The client names itself Moatless, not T3 Code. APP_BASE_NAME falls back to "Moatless" where upstream falls back to "T3 Code", index.html carries the Moatless title and splash labels, and SidebarBrand renders APP_BASE_NAME in place of upstream's T3Wordmark SVG plus its "Code" span — the T3Wordmark function is deleted with it. Everything downstream of APP_BASE_NAME (window title, version-skew copy, auth shells) follows from the one constant, so only these four files carry the delta. Upstream restyles the brand row regularly: take upstream's markup and keep the one APP_BASE_NAME span.

inventory.name: Server-update banner gate
inventory.mustSurvive: The composer never offers to run T3's self-update: the Moatless server does not implement server.updateServer, so the offer and its npx t3 command would point at a command that cannot run. Upstream reaches that offer by two routes and each carries one additive FEATURES.serverUpdateBanner gate in ChatView.tsx: the single-machine composer-banner condition, and the autoUpdateEnvironments memo that feeds useAutoBalanceUpdateBanner. Count the gates every merge — upstream added the second route in #10596, and a gate on one route alone still shows the offer on the other. Holds open the Desktop and host lifecycle gap. Drop the flag and both gates once the backend serves server.updateServer.

inventory.name: Workspace picker gate
inventory.mustSurvive: The composer's context strip offers no workspace choice: Moatless runs a task in its own sandbox and never cuts a git worktree, so "New worktree" and the "Previous worktree" hop name a place a thread cannot go. FEATURES.worktreeSelection is read once in BranchToolbar as showWorkspaceControls, which stands in for upstream's showGitControls at the compact MobileRunContextSelector, the wide group's render condition and its @3xl visibility class, the separator, the BranchToolbarEnvModeSelector, and canUsePreviousWorktree. Gating the compact control whole is deliberate and depends on this build having a single primary environment, so the "Run on" group it shares never renders; a build that grows a second environment has to split that control instead. A draft persisted in "worktree" before the gate would otherwise have no way back out, so two more reads pin the mode to "local": ChatView's envMode, which feeds sendEnvMode and both toolbars, and BranchToolbarBranchSelector's own resolve for the local-draft path that gets no override. Without them a stale draft still asks for a prepareWorktree bootstrap Moatless does not serve, or refuses to send at all over a missing base branch. Drop the flag, all four reads and the showWorkspaceControls alias together once Moatless serves worktrees.

inventory.name: Navigation gates
inventory.mustSurvive: Re-apply list filtering gates. FEATURES.projectManagement also hides the New project affordance wherever it is offered: both sidebars and the draft hero's project picker, which upstream grew a New project menu item on 2026-09-05. A Moatless deployment creates projects from its own admin surfaces, so an enabled New project entry here leads nowhere.

inventory.name: Thread deletion gate in the row menu
inventory.mustSurvive: The row menu never offers Delete: orchestration.dispatchCommand is dispatched as one method, so a thread.delete Moatless does not implement fails generically after the user has already asked for it. One additive FEATURES.threadDeletion spread around upstream's delete item in buildThreadActionMenuItems, which makes archive the tail of the menu — upstream's tests assume delete is. Archive itself is upstream's since 2026-08-16 and is no longer a fork delta.

inventory.name: Settings gates
inventory.mustSurvive: Re-apply route guard and nav/search filtering. General, Appearance, and Providers stay visible except the server-backed add-provider-instance affordance, which lives in ProviderSettingsPanel.tsx since upstream extracted it on 2026-08-08. Every settings page whose controls drive `window.desktopBridge` is listed in FEATURE_BY_SETTINGS_PATH: upstream renders such a page with an "unavailable" notice rather than hiding it, and a hosted build must not list the section at all. `/settings/snap-shot` joined that list when upstream added window capture in #8103.

inventory.name: Moatless REST client
inventory.mustSurvive: Fork-only. The generated client for the Moatless REST API, plus the checked-in OpenAPI description it is generated from and the CI check that the two have not drifted. Regenerate with `vp run --filter @t3tools/moatless-api generate`; do not hand-edit src/generated/**. tsconfig.json turns the @effect/language-service globalFetch diagnostic off for the package — it is deliberately outside Effect, and customInstance.ts calls fetch directly. customInstance.ts also attaches the X-CSRF-Token header the Moatless backend requires on every unsafe method.

inventory.name: Moatless administration reads
inventory.mustSurvive: Fork-only. Caching and dirty-form helpers for the administration pages. Deliberately not createEnvironmentQueryAtomFamily: that helper waits on the environment socket, and administration data is plain HTTP that has no reason to blank on a reconnect. If upstream ships a socket-independent query helper, prefer it and delete query.ts.

inventory.name: Moatless administration pages
inventory.mustSurvive: An administrator reaches every Moatless administration surface from T3 settings — Workspaces, Loops, Integrations, Skills, Secrets and Users, each with its detail route. Built out of upstream's own settings primitives (SettingsSection, SettingsRow, itemRows), so upstream restyling reaches them for free — keep it that way. See the inventory markdown for the markup conventions.

inventory.name: Moatless account credentials page
inventory.mustSurvive: Everyone — not only an administrator — configures their own Claude Code and Codex credentials at /settings/account. The git hosts are the other half of the same question and live at /settings/version-control (moatless-version-control-page). The panel and its logic live under components/settings/moatless/** (moatless-admin-pages' glob), but the page is personal: it must stay out of MOATLESS_ADMIN_PATHS, or the settings.tsx beforeLoad redirects every non-admin away from a page they all need. settingsSearch.ts carries the SettingsPath entry, the SETTINGS_SECTION_LABELS label (first, leading the personal group) and the account-claude and account-codex SETTINGS_SEARCH_ITEMS whose ids the panel's sections anchor to via searchableSetting; SettingsSidebarNav.tsx carries the icon.

inventory.name: Moatless version control page
inventory.mustSurvive: Everyone — not only an administrator — configures their own GitHub and Forgejo credentials at /settings/version-control. Named version-control because upstream already owns /settings/source-control. The panel and its logic live under components/settings/moatless/** (moatless-admin-pages' glob), but the page is personal: it must stay out of MOATLESS_ADMIN_PATHS, or the settings.tsx beforeLoad redirects every non-admin away from a page they all need. settingsSearch.ts carries the SettingsPath entry, the SETTINGS_SECTION_LABELS label (beside Account in the personal group) and the version-control, version-control-github and version-control-forgejo SETTINGS_SEARCH_ITEMS; SettingsSidebarNav.tsx carries the icon, shared with the gated-off /settings/source-control. The page draws one card holding every host, so both host items carry targetId version-control — the panel's only anchor. GitHub's app flow is offered only when the status reports appConnectAvailable, and the PAT form is always offered beside it — a deployment with no GitHub App configured has no other way in. Forgejo is the same shape one level down: it is self-hosted, so the entry lists what GET /api/v1/settings/forgejo/instances reports, draws one section per instance under its host, and names that host in every call. There is no field for typing a host, and adding one back would offer to connect an instance this deployment does not run. It is listed only where the backend's feature-flags read reports forgejo_enabled — the flag gates nothing on the backend, so it is this client that must not offer to connect an instance a deployment does not run. version-control-forgejo carries forgejoEnabledOnly for the same reason, which is why settingsSearch.ts's SettingsSearchItem and SettingsSearchAvailability each carry a fork field and useAvailableSettingsSearchItems.ts reads featureFlagsQuery. The connect callback carries no host, so the entry puts one in the return URL as forgejoHost and reads it back — accountRows.ts's withoutConnectOutcome strips every provider's parameters at once because each entry builds its return URL from the same live URL, and it leaves the route's own entry parameter alone so an OAuth round trip returns to the host the viewer was configuring rather than to GitHub. SettingsMasterDetail.tsx copies the master/detail card out of ProviderSettingsPanel.tsx, which exports none of it; see the settings-master-detail convergence entry.

inventory.name: Browser-defaults settings relocated off /settings/integrations
inventory.mustSurvive: Upstream shipped its own /settings/integrations page on 2026-08-26 (embedded-surface preferences — browser default viewport, zoom, appearance, auto-show floating preview — rendered by IntegrationsSettingsPanel in components/settings/IntegrationsSettings.tsx) at the exact path the fork's Moatless admin Integrations page (moatless-admin-pages) already owned. Resolved by keeping settings.integrations.tsx as the fork's page and moving upstream's page, unmodified, to a new fork-only route at /settings/browser importing the same IntegrationsSettingsPanel. settingsSearch.ts's SettingsPath union, SETTINGS_SECTION_LABELS and every browser-* SETTINGS_SEARCH_ITEMS entry that IntegrationsSettings.tsx anchors, plus SettingsSidebarNav.tsx's icon map, point at /settings/browser instead of /settings/integrations for that panel. Any upstream search item added for that panel needs the same redirect, or the result lands on the fork's admin page and a non-admin viewer is redirected away: browser-profiles, browser-default-profile and browser-link-target arrived on later merges still pointing at /settings/integrations and were corrected on 2026-09-07. settingsSearch.test.ts asserts the route of several of these items, so a redirect made there without the matching test edit fails the web suite. agent-browser-access is the exception — upstream moved that setting to ProjectDefaultsSettings.tsx on /settings/projects on 2026-09-07, which the fork leaves unguarded, so the item points there unmodified. On the next merge, diff upstream's settings.integrations.tsx and IntegrationsSettings.tsx for changes and port them into settings.browser.tsx; the route file is otherwise the entire fork delta here.

inventory.name: Moatless administration nav and guard
inventory.mustSurvive: Converged with Settings gates; the same files carry both deltas and both must survive. Additive: the Administration nav group, the MOATLESS_ADMIN_PATHS entries, the beforeLoad redirect for a non-administrator, and an export on normalizeSearchText. The guard matches detail routes by path prefix — a new administration route with children must be added to MOATLESS_ADMIN_PATHS or it is reachable without an admin check.

inventory.name: Browser frame keyed on the page, not the workspace
inventory.mustSurvive: An HTML page open in the file preview is replaced only when its own bytes change. Upstream keys the frame on the workspace mutation id, which against Moatless means every completed command and every checkpoint throws the page's scroll position and in-page state away. The key falls back to upstream's when the bytes cannot answer it: a PDF is never read, and a failed read has nothing to hash. Known blind spot, deliberate: a page that pulls a sibling stylesheet or script does not reload when the sibling changes — the activity stream cannot say which files a command touched, and nothing on the wire carries a directory revision.

inventory.name: Mermaid diagrams in chat
inventory.mustSurvive: A ```mermaid fence in a chat message is drawn as a diagram rather than highlighted as source. The whole delta in upstream's ChatMarkdown.tsx is two imports and one early return above upstream's own return in the `pre` renderer; the diagram sits inside upstream's MarkdownCodeBlock so the header, the language label and the copy button stay upstream's and copy still copies the mermaid source. The fence falls back to that same highlighted source in every case the diagram is not there — while the message streams, while mermaid loads, when mermaid cannot parse the source, and when someone asks for the source back — so a mermaid fence never renders worse than upstream renders it. Four properties are load-bearing and easy to lose in a rewrite: mermaid is imported lazily, because it is around a megabyte and nobody who never sees a diagram should pay for it; renders are serialized, because `initialize` sets the theme globally; rendered SVG is cached and read during the first render, because the message list is virtualized and a scrolled-back diagram would otherwise flash its source; and `securityLevel` is `strict`, because the source is model-written and arrives over the wire.

inventory.name: Recently used gate in the browser empty state
inventory.mustSurvive: The browser's empty state never offers a "Recently used" URL. Browser history is keyed by project and read by every thread of that project, while a thread server's URL names the sandbox of the task that raised it (https://task--5733.…), so one thread's entries point every other thread at a sandbox it does not own and at a host that stops with that task. One additive FEATURES.browserHistory gate on the recentEntries prop PreviewView hands PreviewEmptyState. The gate sits at that call site rather than inside PreviewEmptyState deliberately: the component and upstream's three recents tests in PreviewEmptyState.test.tsx stay at zero delta, and the fork hands it an empty list instead. browserHistoryStore still records visits and titles, and PreviewView's title effect still reads useThreadRecentHistory — this gates the surface, not the writes. Drop the flag and the gate once a recorded entry can name a page a second thread of the project can reach.

convergence.name: Auth
convergence.watchFor: No convergence expected; auth is fork-owned.

convergence.name: Dev proxy / single-origin
convergence.watchFor: Work on DEV_PROXIED_PATH_PREFIXES, T3CODE_SINGLE_ORIGIN_DEV, or resolveDevProxyTarget.
convergence.action: Take upstream and re-apply only Web Vite Delta.

convergence.name: Allowed hosts
convergence.action: Drop the T3CODE_ALLOWED_HOSTS alias once deployments inject upstream's name.

convergence.name: Thread servers
convergence.watchFor: Any upstream concept of a server owned by a thread, especially in WS_METHODS.
convergence.action: Prefer upstream; remove fork group, stubs first.

convergence.name: Unsupported methods
convergence.watchFor: An optional-method marker, handshake metadata, ServerConfig, or an HTTP metadata endpoint — a general way for a server to say it does not serve a method.
convergence.action: Prefer upstream semantics and collapse the error-union entries into it.

convergence.name: Surface gating
convergence.watchFor: New booleans on ExecutionEnvironmentCapabilities. Upstream adds one per thread-lifecycle surface — threadSettlement, threadSnooze, threadPinning and threadPinReorder as of 2026-08-08.
convergence.action: Prefer upstream's capability where one exists and delete the matching FEATURES flag. The server decides, so the surface then follows the backend without a fork edit.

convergence.name: Where a thread's pull requests come from
convergence.watchFor: Upstream giving the `+N` badge a surface of its own, or folding a pull-request event into the thread detail — a `thread.pull-request-linked` or `-unlinked` frame a reducer applies — or `pullRequests` moving off the thread snapshot into a subscription of its own.
convergence.action: Take upstream's pull-request surfaces whole, except the badge popover named in the inventory entry. Keep only the `pullRequests` line in `mergeEnvironmentThread`, and delete it the day Moatless emits a link event a reducer can apply (see `docs/fork/gaps.md`, _A pull request link is a listing change, not an event_). An event upstream ships is not that day: the gap is the backend emitting one.

convergence.name: Web on a phone
convergence.watchFor: A swipeable mobile sidebar, a touch affordance for thread-row actions, or a contextMenuFallback rewritten on a popup primitive.
convergence.action: Prefer upstream and drop the matching part of Mobile Touch Delta.

convergence.name: Fences rendered as something other than source
convergence.watchFor: Any per-language branch in the `pre` renderer, a fence-renderer registry, or a mermaid dependency in apps/web.
convergence.action: Prefer upstream's, delete fork/mermaidDiagram* and drop Mermaid Diagram Delta. A registry upstream owns is also the place to move this to rather than keeping the branch.

convergence.name: Send while a turn is running
convergence.watchFor: Upstream widening showSendWhileRunning past isMobileViewport in ChatComposer.tsx, or dropping the prop and always rendering send beside stop.
convergence.action: Take upstream. The fork's own rule was dropped on 2026-08-16 when upstream shipped the prop; a phone browser is a mobile viewport, so the fork's case is served.

convergence.name: Message provenance
convergence.watchFor: Any upstream field on OrchestrationMessage saying a message did not come from the composer — an origin, author, or source.
convergence.action: Prefer upstream's shape, re-point the chip at it, and drop the fork field.

convergence.name: Searchable settings list
convergence.watchFor: Upstream lifting the expandable header search out of KeybindingsSettings.tsx into a shared settings component, or giving SettingsSection a search affordance of its own.

convergence.name: Settings master/detail card
convergence.watchFor: An export of the list-beside-editor card from ProviderSettingsPanel.tsx or settingsLayout.tsx — today providerCardClassName, providerCardHeightClassName and the lg:grid-cols-[17rem_minmax(0,1fr)] grid are private to that panel, and components/settings/moatless/SettingsMasterDetail.tsx is a copy of them.
convergence.action: Drop the copy and point VersionControlPanel.tsx at upstream's primitive. Until then an upstream restyle of ProviderSettingsPanel does not reach the Version control page, so re-copy the classes by eye.
